title: Yellowstone: The World’s First National Park

source.name: VOA Learning English — Yellowstone: The World’s First National Park
source.license: Nội dung của VOA (Voice of America), phạm vi công cộng
source.note: Giữ nguyên nội dung các đoạn chính; bỏ tiêu đề nhỏ.

paras: Yellowstone National Park in the western United States was the world’s first national park.
Established in 1872, it is famous for its geothermal activity and wild animals. It includes beautiful mountains, deep canyons, lakes and rivers.
Yellowstone is still one of the largest national parks in the U.S. It takes up almost 9,000 square kilometers. Most of the park lies within the western state of Wyoming.
The park is unusual because of what lies underneath it. It sits on top of an ancient super volcano, known as the Yellowstone Caldera. The caldera remains an active volcano.

A lake of hot liquid rock is about six kilometers under the park. Experts say this lake is under huge amounts of pressure. The pressure and heat cause geysers to shoot hot water out of the ground and mud to boil at Yellowstone.

The park is home to more than 300 geysers. There are more geysers and hot springs in Yellowstone than any other place on Earth. “Old Faithful” is the name of the park’s most famous geyser because it erupts about every 90 minutes.

Yellowstone is on a high plateau with an average height of 2,400 meters above sea level. This makes the weather very cold in winter, with January temperatures averaging between -18 degrees and -7 degrees Celsius. However, some areas of the park remain open to visitors throughout the year.

Yellowstone Canyon is about 365 meters deep. The Yellowstone River runs through it and drops 93 meters in the Lower Falls. Visitors can walk on a path that brings them very close to the top of the falls. There, they can see and hear the powerful falls.
In summer of 1988, forest fires burned large areas of the park. Most of those areas are now covered with plants and young trees.

Yellowstone is home to the largest group of wild animals in the lower 48 United States. These include bison, grizzly bear, elk, deer, moose, fox, beaver, coyote and wolves. In 2024, park officials estimated the bison population to be about 4,500 animals. That makes it the largest group of wild bison in the world.
There is still a wild west in America…and its name is Yellowstone.

questions.q: What does the writer say makes Yellowstone unusual?
options: It contains more lakes than any other park in the country
It lies above a volcano that is still active
It stays open to visitors in every area all year round
It is the largest protected area anywhere in the world
questions.explain: Đoạn 4: công viên nằm trên một siêu núi lửa cổ và “remains an active volcano”.

questions.q: According to experts, what causes the geysers and boiling mud?
options: Intense heat and pressure from molten rock far below the surface
Water from melting snow that flows through the canyon
Earthquakes along the line of the Yellowstone River
Hot summer weather that warms the lakes in the park
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: hồ đá nóng chảy sâu 6 km chịu áp suất lớn; “pressure and heat cause geysers”.

questions.q: Why is Old Faithful the best-known geyser in the park?
options: It throws water higher than any other geyser does
It was the first geyser that visitors ever saw
It is located closest to the entrance of the park
Its eruptions come at fairly regular intervals
questions.explain: Đoạn 6: nổi tiếng vì phun “about every 90 minutes” — khá đều đặn (tên “Faithful”).

questions.q: What explains the very cold winters in Yellowstone?
options: Cold air collects inside the deep canyon
The park sits on high ground
Many lakes and rivers freeze completely
Strong winds blow from nearby mountains
questions.explain: Đoạn 7: nằm trên cao nguyên trung bình 2.400 m nên mùa đông rất lạnh.

questions.q: What can be concluded from the information about winter in the park?
options: The park does not close entirely, even in severe cold
No visitors can enter between December and February
Temperatures in January are warmer than in summer
Only the canyon is open to the public during winter
questions.explain: Đoạn 7: tháng 1 lạnh nhất (−18 đến −7 °C) nhưng “some areas … remain open … throughout the year”.

questions.q: What does the writer say about the bison in Yellowstone?
options: Their numbers have fallen below one thousand
They are the only large animals that live in the park
The park has the biggest wild herd of them in the world
They are kept in a special area away from visitors
questions.explain: Đoạn 10: ước tính khoảng 4.500 con, “largest group of wild bison in the world”.

questions.q: Most of the areas damaged by the fires of 1988 are still bare.
questions.explain: Đoạn 9: phần lớn khu vực bị cháy nay đã phủ cây cỏ và cây non.

questions.q: Yellowstone has more visitors in summer than in winter.
questions.explain: Bài không đưa số liệu du khách theo mùa.
